title: Handle blank Geek+ RMS page by using API Dog or database to see what is on the screen (thin-client visibility limitation)
summary: When the Geek+ RMS web page (Overall System RMS) appears blank—e.g., because the firewall is not open—or when support personnel are limited by thin-client visibility, use the source-stated alternatives (API Dog or the database) to retrieve the same RMS-relevant information that would have been shown on the screen (system faults on the left and active AGV faults on the right).
when_to_use: Use this when the Geek+ RMS “Overall System RMS” page should show RMS content but instead shows blank due to firewall restrictions, and/or when thin clients prevent direct viewing of what is on the RMS screen.
roles_and_responsibilities: L2_support: Retrieve RMS-relevant fault/metrics visibility using the source-stated alternatives (API Dog or the database) when the Geek+ RMS page is blank.
L2_support: Confirm the retrieved information matches the expected RMS content areas (system faults on the left; active AGV faults on the right) to determine what the RMS screen would have shown.
access_or_tools_needed: API Dog (as named by the source)
Database access (as named by the source)
Geek+ RMS web page (to confirm blank state)

access_required: Access to API Dog (as named by the source)
Access to the database (as named by the source)
Access to the Geek+ RMS web location to attempt viewing the page
system_preconditions: The Geek+ RMS page is expected to show RMS content but is blank (e.g., firewall not open / thin-client visibility limitation).

visual_references.description: Overall System RMS page description: firewall not open leads to blank page; expected RMS content areas include system faults (left) and active AGV faults (right).

steps.title: Attempt to view the Geek+ RMS page (“Overall System RMS”)
steps.purpose: Establish whether the RMS page is blank so you can apply the source-stated visibility workaround.
steps.instruction: Open the Geek+ RMS web application and navigate to the “Overall System RMS” page (the page that should show RMS content).
steps.expected_result: The “Overall System RMS” page is blank (or otherwise not showing the expected RMS content).
steps.healthy_condition: The page shows RMS content (system faults on the left and active AGV faults on the right).
steps.failure_condition: The page shows blank content when it should display RMS information.

actions.label: Check Overall System RMS page state
actions.exact_action: View the Geek+ RMS page (“Overall System RMS”).

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: This page should show RMS, but the firewall is not open, so it just kind of shows blank.
will also show system faults on the left and any == mm - active AGV faults on the right.

steps.title: Interpret blank RMS as a firewall-not-open / thin-client visibility issue (not a system condition)
steps.purpose: Avoid misdiagnosing the blank page as a fleet/system fault when the source attributes it to firewall/visibility limitations.
steps.instruction: If the “Overall System RMS” page is blank, treat it as the source-stated visibility limitation (firewall not open and/or thin-client inability to view) rather than concluding that the system has no faults.
steps.expected_result: You proceed to retrieve RMS-relevant information using API Dog or the database rather than relying on the blank web page.
steps.healthy_condition: Your next action is to use API Dog or the database to obtain the RMS-relevant fault/metrics visibility.
steps.failure_condition: You rely only on the blank RMS page and do not retrieve RMS-relevant information via API Dog or the database.

actions.label: Classify blank page cause per source
actions.exact_action: Interpret this per the source as a firewall-not-open visibility issue (rather than a system condition).

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: This page should show RMS, but the firewall is not open, so it just kind of shows blank.
Because they’re on thin clients, we can’t see our mess; we’re kind of dependent on either pulling an API, an API dog, or using the database to see what’s on their screen.

steps.title: Retrieve RMS-relevant information via API Dog or the database
steps.purpose: Recover visibility into what the RMS screen would have shown despite blank/thin-client limitations.
steps.instruction: Use one of the source-stated alternatives to retrieve what is on the RMS screen: (1) pull via API Dog, or (2) use the database to see what’s on their screen.
steps.expected_result: You obtain RMS-relevant information that corresponds to the RMS screen content areas (system faults on the left; active AGV faults on the right).
steps.healthy_condition: API Dog/database retrieval returns data that can be mapped to system faults (left) and active AGV faults (right).
steps.failure_condition: API Dog/database retrieval is not possible or returns no data.

actions.label: Pull RMS visibility via API Dog
actions.exact_action: Pull an API (API dog) to see what’s on their screen.

actions.exact_action: Use the database to see what’s on their screen.

stop_or_escalate_if: If API Dog/database retrieval is not possible or returns no data, stop and escalate (the source only provides these two alternatives for visibility when direct viewing is limited).

steps.title: Confirm retrieved data matches expected RMS content areas (system faults left; active AGV faults right)
steps.purpose: Validate that the retrieved API/database information corresponds to what the RMS screen would have displayed.
steps.instruction: Compare the retrieved information to the expected RMS content areas described by the source: system faults on the left and active AGV faults on the right.
steps.expected_result: You can confirm presence/absence of system faults and active AGV faults using the retrieved data, even though the RMS web page is blank.
steps.healthy_condition: Retrieved data clearly indicates system faults (left area equivalent) and active AGV faults (right area equivalent).
steps.failure_condition: Retrieved data cannot be mapped to the expected RMS content areas (system faults vs active AGV faults).

success_criteria: Even with a blank Geek+ RMS “Overall System RMS” page, you obtain RMS-relevant information via API Dog or the database.
You can confirm presence/absence of system faults and active AGV faults using the retrieved information mapped to the RMS content areas (left vs right).
healthy_conditions: Geek+ RMS “Overall System RMS” page is blank due to firewall/thin-client limitation, but API Dog/database retrieval returns RMS-relevant fault information.
Retrieved information corresponds to system faults (left) and active AGV faults (right).
failure_conditions: Geek+ RMS page is blank and API Dog/database retrieval is not possible or returns no data.
Retrieved information cannot be interpreted/mapped to system faults (left) and active AGV faults (right).
escalation_guidance: If API Dog/database retrieval is not possible or returns no data, stop and escalate, since the source only provides these two alternatives for visibility when direct viewing is limited.
